close_reason: Resolved by the same commit 4ec9135 as bd:JMAP-sgrr.14. The crate-level rustdoc 'Design: numeric-range bounds are not type-enforced' section's table lists Directory.list_as and PersonalInfo.list_as alongside the pref sites and PartialDate.month/day; README Gotchas bullet consolidates all four findings. Option<NonZeroU32> was the type-level alternative but per parent sgrr.17 family decision (doc-only hardening), the kit does not take that public-API break.
description:
Two fields carry the 'must be > 0' constraint per RFC 9553:

- Directory.list_as at lib.rs:770 (doc-comment 'Must be > 0 when set.', RFC 9553
  §2.6.2)
- PersonalInfo.list_as at lib.rs:1110 (doc-comment 'Must be > 0 when set.',
  RFC 9553 §2.8.4)

Both are typed Option<u32>. A caller can construct .list_as = Some(0), serialize
the wire-invalid object, and have it round-trip. No validation, no Result-returning
constructor. Every consumer enforcing the constraint writes the same is_zero check.

The textbook Rust fix is Option<NonZeroU32>. That makes Some(0) impossible to
construct at the type level and gives the caller a free conversion via
NonZeroU32::new(n). Cost: every caller building these fields wraps their u32
in NonZeroU32::new(...).expect(...) or matches on it; the type system pays them
back by catching the bug at compile time.

This is breaking once 1.0 lands, so do it now if doing it.
title: list_as fields are Option<u32> but RFC 9553 says 'must be > 0' — should be NonZeroU32
